20 mins daily of HIIT on the rowing machine can be a game changer : 1.	Burn calories in a fun fast way.   In 20 minutes, you can get a high-output session that hits hard without needing a long workout — working at 80-95% of your Max Effort it scales for wherever you are at. 2.	Build full-body fitness.   Rowing works your legs, glutes, core, back, and arms all at once, so you’re training more than just cardio. 3.	Boost heart and lung power.   HIIT pushes your aerobic engine, helping you get fitter, recover faster and feel less gassed in hard fast efforts. 4.	Improve endurance and work capacity.   The repeated intervals teach your body to handle intensity better.  Over time consistency builds and you can play with the variables of recovery.  The benefits carries over to other sport, training and everyday energy. 5.	Time-efficient and low-impact.   You get a brutal session in a short window and the rower is easier on the joints which has been a an absolute game changer. P.S so many wonderful messages about people starting to use the rowing machine more! I’ll be dropping some core workouts that I incorporate that have helped me develop an elite level of endurance and cardio and keep myself in shape. This rowing machine and mentality of rowing training can really make something out of you if you commit! #rowing #hiit #dailyworkout #routine #fitness

It’s creamy and refreshing!☀️ • ingredients for one serving: 1/2 ripe mango  2 tablespoons kefir juice of 1/2 small lime optional: a drizzle of maple syrup or honey for extra sweetness • 1. Cut the mango in half, remove the pit and scoop out a small hole in the center. Cover the mango half with plastic wrap and freeze overnight 2. Let sit at room temperature for 10-15 minutes 3. Add the kefir and lime juice to the center. Start scraping the mango flesh and mixing everything together. Once you've scraped out all the mango, you'll have a creamy ice cream. Testing VIRAL watermelon ice cream! (it's messy) ✨Recipe: Ingredients: • 1 personal-sized watermelon • ½ cup Heavy cream Directions: 1. Slice the watermelon in half and scoop out flesh from the center, leaving a thick layer attached to the rind to create a natural bowl. 2. Place the watermelon halves in the freezer overnight, or until completely frozen. 3. Pour about ½ cup of heavy cream into the center of one frozen watermelon half. Using a sturdy spoon, continuously scrape the frozen fruit while churning the cream until it transforms into a smooth, soft ice cream-like texture. 4. Scoop into bowls or enjoy it straight from the watermelon for a refreshing homemade frozen treat! 🍉

I went to korea's first maid cafe in hongdae to understand why there is a massive demand for these spaces in Seoul.  there was a food or beverage minimum (starting around ₩9,000 / $7.50), and you are forbidden from directly filming the maids' faces. the experience can be a social anxiety simulator for introverts - you have to make cat sounds to call the maids and cast a spell (moe moe kyun) on your food before you can even eat!  the maids were incredibly warm and skilled at active listening; we played games and had deep conversations with one maid who is a philosophy major. it feels like we paid for undivided, warm human connection.  would you try this? #seoul #hongdae #maidcafe #moemoekyun #japan #koreanculture #hongdaeboys
